sources.title: openvla/openvla on GitHub (README)
sources.covers: the centre crop at test time for augmented fine-tunes, no action chunking, the suggested control rate

note: OpenVLA resizes each image to 224 × 224 without keeping its aspect ratio ("resize-naive", no letterbox) and feeds it to two ViTs with 14 px patches (DINOv2 and SigLIP, features concatenated channel-wise). The README adds that a model fine-tuned with image augmentation (--image_aug True) expects "the center 90% crop" at test time (90 % of the area: about 94.9 % of each side); for such a model, override crop_rule with center_crop_resize and crop_side_fraction 0.949. Tokens per image are not stated (the paper says only that "higher-resolution images result in more image patch tokens"). The control rate is not one figure: the paper uses 5 Hz and 15 Hz controllers. Code MIT; the weights may carry the Llama 2 Community License (README). DexVantage bundles these figures only, not the model.

input_resolution.quote: "image_sizes": [224, 224]; the paper: "We thus opt for a resolution of 224×224px for the final OpenVLA model."

crop_side_fraction.quote: No crop for the released model; see the note for augmented fine-tunes.

n_cameras.quote: the model "currently only supports single-image observations"

action_chunk.quote: "OpenVLA is not trained with action chunking"; the paper calls it a "single-step policy"

execute_steps.quote: one action per inference (no action chunking)

inference_ms.quote: "runs at approximately 6Hz on one NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU" (1000 / 6 = 166.7 ms); with 4-bit quantisation "can run at 3Hz on the A5000"

control_hz.quote: Not one figure: "5Hz and 15 Hz non-blocking controllers" (Franka-Tabletop, Franka-DROID) and a 5 Hz controller for BridgeData V2 (paper); "Collect at a control frequency around 5-10Hz" (README).
